findings.statement: CA9 transcripts in tumour are almost entirely tumour-cell derived, with RCC cells holding nearly all of them [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], while only about half of RCC cells express it [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=54.7]; the bulk signal is tumour-intrinsic and CA9 is the top convergence-ranked gene, but it is already clinically drugged (girentuximab) and expression is heterogeneous across tumour cells.

Paired tumour-cell versus proximal-tubule pseudobulk shows CA9 strongly up in tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739], and in Visium the high-CA9 spots are enriched for RCC neighbours [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381] (macrophages show only a marginal enrichment), consistent with a tumour-cell niche marker.

The AlphaFold CA9 model has mean pLDDT [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56] and its top detected cavity has volume [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] A3 with one nearby accessible lysine; detected cavities recover half of experimental ligand-contact residues [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5], which only validates cavity detection and says nothing about degron or ligase compatibility.

MET is mainly tumour-cell derived in tumour tissue, with RCC cells holding most transcripts [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935], but only a minority of RCC cells express it [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=35.2], and endothelium carries a smaller per-cell share, so MET is a tumour-cell target with heterogeneous expression.

KDR is an endothelial gene, not a tumour-cell target: endothelial cells hold almost all transcripts [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], and a substantial fraction of endothelial cells express it [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=40.5]; anti-VEGFR therapy acts on the vasculature.

In this scRNA-seq dataset EPAS1 (HIF2A) transcripts sit mostly outside RCC cells: endothelial cells hold a large share [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.365] against a small share for RCC cells [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.051], so mRNA level in bulk is not a tumour-cell readout (HIF2A activity is better read through targets such as CA9).

CD74 is an antigen-presenting-cell and lymphocyte transcript, not tumour-cell: macrophages hold 0.436 of tumour transcripts [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436], with dendritic cells showing the highest per-cell level and nearly all of them expressing it, so it is a microenvironment marker.

CXCR4 is carried by infiltrating lymphocytes: CD8 T cells hold 0.563 of tumour transcripts [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD8_T; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563] and CD4 T, B and pDC cells also express it; it is an immune-axis target, not tumour-intrinsic.

Tumour track: COL23A1 is made mainly by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], stays up when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], replicates in TCGA-KIRC, has no clinical drug, a surface call of surface (UniProt cell membrane; SURFY and CSPA do not support it), a few ccRCC papers, and no protein enrichment in vital-organ proteome; the AlphaFold model is low confidence (see model record) with one tiny cavity, no dependency (DepMap not selective) and no prognostic signal, so it remains a hypothesis.

Tumour track: RAB42 is expressed mostly by RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], persists in a pure tumour [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189] and replicates in TCGA, with very few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug; its location is unknown for antibody access (UniProt membrane, not in SURFY or CSPA), survival is not associated and no dependency is shown, so it is an unvalidated hypothesis.

Stroma track: OLFML2A is a fibroblast-derived secreted protein [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647], purity-robust [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527] and TCGA-replicated with no clinical drug, but it is a microenvironment target with notable colon expression, no survival association and no functional evidence.

Stroma track: JAG2 is a surface Notch ligand made mainly by endothelium [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487], replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, with no clinical drug; it is less novel than other candidates (several ccRCC papers), has modest fold change, heart-muscle RNA expression, and no dependency evidence.

Immune track: MILR1 is a surface macrophage (mast-cell receptor family) gene with no ccRCC papers, with most tumour transcripts in macrophages [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.841]; its bulk increase largely vanishes in a pure tumour [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414], flagged infiltration-driven, although TCGA shows adverse prognosis; it is a macrophage-state marker hypothesis, not a tumour-cell target.

Immune track: GAL3ST4 is almost exclusively macrophage [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.972] and is TCGA-replicated with adverse prognosis, but it is an internal Golgi enzyme (not antibody-accessible) and its fold change extrapolated to a pure tumour is small [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401], so at most a macrophage biomarker.

caveats: Single-cell data come from 12 donors; some cell groups (endothelium, fibroblasts, PT) come from few donors, so shares are approximate.
Transcript shares depend on how many cells of each type were captured; per-cell comparisons should use cpm_share.
Structural scores are descriptive monomer heuristics and do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or predict degradation.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses with literature counted by gene symbol; none has functional or dependency evidence, and DepMap shows no selective dependency for the ones quoted.
CD70, SCARB1, NNMT, COXFA4L2 and other top convergence genes were not profiled at cell level here for lack of budget; CD70 and the EGFR gene were not examined.
Spatial enrichment was run for CA9 only.
